If installation is unavailable

You can use ChatGPT in a browser for text-based exercises, or pair with a colleague. Check the download page for current system requirements; contact your IT support if a managed computer blocks installation.

Next · Configure the access you need

Connect AI to your working environment.

Access to the right browser, app, or document can reduce copying and pasting and let AI help carry out a task. Open ChatGPT’s Settings and review the three areas below. Enable the capabilities that support what you want to do.

Start with your task. Choose the resources it needs, review the requested permissions, and try a small example. You do not need every switch turned on. The screenshots show the presenter’s setup, not a required configuration.
Browser Work with web pages inside ChatGPT
Settings → Browser

Enable Browser if you want ChatGPT to operate its built-in browser—for example, to inspect the workshop page we are creating.

  • Local URL open destination: choose ChatGPT if you want local web previews to open inside the app.
  • Web URL and link open destination: choose where ordinary links open. This is a navigation preference, not permission to control every site.
  • Annotation screenshots: include them when visual feedback is useful; the setting notes that they increase plan usage.

The built-in browser is separate from your regular Chrome profile. Chrome access is configured under Computer use below.

Official browser guide ↗

Plugins Connect the services and tools you use
Settings → Plugins

Review installed plugins and enable the ones relevant to your task. Use the Plugins directory to install a missing plugin.

  • Google Drive or Notion: work with documents in a connected account.
  • GitHub: work with repositories and project materials.
  • Gmail, Calendar, or Slack: work with communication or scheduling information when needed.

A plugin switch may not complete setup. Connect the intended account and review its requested access, then start a new chat to try it. These services provide cloud access; they do not automatically grant access to all files on your computer.

Official plugin guide ↗

Computer use Let AI work with desktop apps
Settings → Computer use

Enable Any App when your task needs visual interaction with a desktop app. If prompted, install or enable the Computer Use plugin in ChatGPT Work or Codex.

  • Google Chrome: follow the installation prompts for the browser extension. Use the browser profile where it is installed; select Manage to review website access. The toggle alone does not grant every site access.
  • Microsoft Excel: enable it and follow any add-in setup prompts when your task needs control of an open workbook.
  • Mac: review Screen Recording and Accessibility requests so the tool can see and operate the intended app. Windows: keep the target app visible; computer use can take over the active desktop.

Review Always-allowed apps before saving ongoing access. For this live workshop, leave Locked use off; it is unnecessary for the exercises.

Computer use guide ↗   ·   Browser extension setup ↗

Check one connection before the event.

Choose one capability, open an appropriate example, and ask for a small, clearly scoped task. For example, after enabling Browser:

“Use the built-in browser to open https://acros.umbc.edu/ and tell me the group’s research focus. Do not change anything.”

These are Mac screenshots supplied by the presenter on September 13, 2026. Menus and availability can differ by app version, operating system, plan, region, and institutional settings. File and folder permissions remain separate. With other AI apps, follow the same approach: identify the needed resource, review access, and test it. Keep student records and confidential research out of workshop examples.

Optional · Build your toolkit

Give your AI collaborator more tools.

These tools help with local analysis, document processing, and clear visual feedback. Choose what fits your work; none is required for the core workshop. Installing a package does not itself give AI access to your computer—it still needs the appropriate permissions and working environment.

01 / Mac · Package manager

Homebrew

A convenient way to install and update command-line programs that an AI assistant can use for tasks such as processing PDFs or converting video.

  1. Visit brew.sh and follow its Mac installation instructions.
  2. Complete the installer’s “Next steps,” including Terminal setup if requested.
  3. Open a new Terminal and run brew --version to check it.

Example: brew install poppler adds PDF utilities. Install additional tools when a task calls for them.

Homebrew installation ↗
02 / Mac & Windows · Analysis

Anaconda + Jupyter

Anaconda Distribution provides Python, package management, and notebook tools. Use Jupyter to keep code, explanations, and figures together for research or teaching.

  1. Download the installer matching your computer and follow the setup prompts.
  2. Open Anaconda Navigator and launch JupyterLab.
  3. Create a notebook and run print("Hello, AI cowork!").

Already have a working Python setup? Keep it. Create a separate environment for workshop experiments. Use Anaconda’s education guidance to check academic access.

Download Anaconda ↗Academic access ↗Jupyter guide ↗
03 / Everyone · Visual feedback

Screenshots with annotations

Circle a confusing equation, point to a layout problem, or mark the part of a figure you want to discuss. Share the image with a precise request.

  1. Mac: press Shift–Command–5 to capture. Click the thumbnail to mark it up, or open the image in Preview and use Markup for arrows, shapes, and text.
  2. Windows: press Windows–Shift–S, capture a region, then open it in Snipping Tool to annotate with the pen or highlighter.

Try: “Explain the equation I circled and define each symbol.” Crop out unrelated content before sharing.

Preview: documents are private. The promotion package and generated example letter are not available for public download yet. You can explore the demonstration and copy the prompts below.

Your example prompt
I am a full professor in a prestigious university. Recently, I received a request for a recommendation letter from UMBC for a faculty member named Zhibo Zhang. I am not a collaborator of this faculty member, and I will evaluate his achievements, research, teaching, and service based on the materials submitted to me.

Can you read through the materials in the folder and draft an anonymous recommendation letter for Dr. Zhang? Please comment on three areas, research, teaching, and service, giving research the most weight.
Add the source and output instructions
Use only the submitted materials; do not search online. Create the letter as a downloadable Word (.docx) file. Do not invent facts, an evaluator’s name or university affiliation, or personal knowledge of Dr. Zhang. If you cannot read a file, tell me which one.
Then ask

“For each major claim, identify the supporting file and passage. Separate documented achievements from your assessment, and revise anything the materials do not support.”

Check together

Are research contributions described accurately? Are team achievements attributed fairly? Does the teaching assessment reflect the actual evaluations? Does the letter avoid inventing an evaluator’s identity or relationship?

Start with file upload and document creation. Homebrew and Anaconda are optional for this exercise. If direct folder access is unavailable, attach the documents; if the older .doc CV cannot be read, provide a PDF or .docx version.

More examples to explore together

Research / Reading

Turn a paper into a conversation.

Bring a public paper or paste a short excerpt. Keep the original nearby so you can check the response.

A starting prompt
Using only the paper or excerpt I provide, identify the research question, the approach, and the main finding. Separate the authors’ evidence from their interpretation. Point me to the relevant sections or passages, and say when the supplied text does not support an answer. End with three questions for a journal-club discussion.
Then ask

“Which conclusion depends most on an assumption? Explain the assumption and show where it appears in the text.”

Check together

Compare the response with the paper. Do the cited passages support each claim? Were any limitations left out?

A useful habit: ask for the next improvement you need. Your disciplinary judgment guides the conversation.

This worksheet runs in your browser and does not send your entries anywhere. Entries are not saved automatically; use “Save as text” before closing the page. Use public or synthetic material for the exercise and follow your institution’s rules for sensitive information.
